bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced an AddressSanitizer stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 15 in `ot::MeshCoP::DatasetManager::HandleSet`. The staged 89-byte `ip6-send-fuzzer` witness carries CoAP URI `c/as` and a Mesh Local Prefix TLV header `07 0f`. In `DatasetManager::HandleSet`, `Tlv::GetTlv(aMessage, Tlv::kMeshLocalPrefix, sizeof(meshLocalPrefix), meshLocalPrefix)` copies only 10 bytes into stack local `MeshLocalPrefixTlv meshLocalPrefix` (the 2-byte TLV header plus the fixed 8-byte `otMeshLocalPrefix`) but preserves the advertised length 15 in the copied header. `meshLocalPrefix.IsValid()` still accepts that object because it only requires a length of at least 8. The subsequent connectivity check calls `memcmp(&meshLocalPrefix.GetMeshLocalPrefix(), &Get<Mle::MleRouter>().GetMeshLocalPrefix(), meshLocalPrefix.GetLength())`, so `memcmp()` reads 15 bytes from an 8-byte field and overreads adjacent stack memory. The patch fixes the bug by replacing `meshLocalPrefix.GetLength()` with `meshLocalPrefix.GetMeshLocalPrefixLength()`, a fixed 8-byte bound.

root_cause.description: The compare bound comes from the attacker-controlled TLV header instead of the fixed 8-byte Mesh Local Prefix field size. The patch replaces this expression with `meshLocalPrefix.GetMeshLocalPrefixLength()`.
root_cause.note: `ot::Tlv::Get()` preserved the header length 15 inside `meshLocalPrefix` even though only `sizeof(meshLocalPrefix) == 10` bytes were copied into the stack object. Reusing that header length here is the missing size obligation that makes the later `memcmp()` overread.

parser_admitted.description: The CoAP parser has already reconstructed URI path `c/as` from the request options, matched the active-dataset set resource, and is dispatching into `ActiveDataset::HandleSet()`.

coarse_trace.summary: The CoAP request parser reconstructs URI path `c/as` from the message options, matches the active-dataset set resource, and dispatches the request to `ActiveDataset::HandleSet()`.
The active-dataset handler forwards the admitted request into `DatasetManager::HandleSet()`.

The Mesh Local Prefix TLV is copied into stack local `meshLocalPrefix` with advertised length 15, `IsValid()` accepts it, and `memcmp()` uses that header length instead of the fixed 8-byte prefix size, producing the observed ASan stack-buffer-overflow READ.

fine_trace.note: The MeshCoP parser finds the request's Mesh Local Prefix TLV and copies it into stack local `meshLocalPrefix`. In the staged witness the payload bytes at offsets 71-72 are `07 0f`, so `ot::Tlv::Get()` first reads a header with type `kMeshLocalPrefix` and length 15, then re-reads only `sizeof(meshLocalPrefix) == 10` bytes total. The copied object therefore keeps header length 15 but only contains the 2-byte TLV header plus the fixed 8-byte `otMeshLocalPrefix` field.

The validity gate accepts the oversized TLV because `MeshLocalPrefixTlv::IsValid()` only requires `GetLength() >= sizeof(*this) - sizeof(Tlv)`. With stored length 15 and fixed field size 8, this condition is true, so the short-circuit `if` continues into the connectivity comparison instead of rejecting the malformed length.

Root cause. The compare bound is taken directly from the TLV header copied in step 1, so this expression yields 15 instead of the fixed Mesh Local Prefix size 8 (`OT_MESH_LOCAL_PREFIX_SIZE`). The patch replaces this value with `meshLocalPrefix.GetMeshLocalPrefixLength()`, which returns `sizeof(mMeshLocalPrefix)`.

`memcmp()` begins at the embedded 8-byte `mMeshLocalPrefix` field inside stack local `meshLocalPrefix` and reads 15 bytes because of step 3. Once the comparison advances past the eighth byte, it reads adjacent stack memory beyond `meshLocalPrefix`; AddressSanitizer reports `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 15` at this call and names `meshLocalPrefix` (line 85) as the overrun object.

format.name: OpenThread ip6-send MeshCoP active-dataset request
format.contract: Exactly the staged 89-byte witness: the first byte is the harness link-security flag, and the remaining bytes form an IPv6/CoAP request that reaches URI `c/as` and contains MeshCoP TLV bytes `07 0f` at offsets 71-72 of the fuzz input. That layout makes `Tlv::GetTlv(..., kMeshLocalPrefix, sizeof(meshLocalPrefix), ...)` copy a `MeshLocalPrefixTlv` whose header length is 15 even though only the fixed 8-byte prefix field fits in `meshLocalPrefix`. The staged artifacts do not justify a broader trigger class beyond this witnessed layout.
